en: Finally, you have a grudge.
You made a mess,
People don't go anywhere
You touched the horse yesterday.
Cattle hunting, butchering meat,
You have become a sinner.
Select cattle from the cattle,
People take ore abroad,
Thank you for my bravery
He was surprised that he was interested.
My blood in the guard,
Kill your soul.
Feasting on the booty without a clue,
You took so much of my property,
You killed all my wrestlers.
Reducing me to a smokeless ember,
You have set my soul ablaze,
You have drained away my strength.
You carried off as plunder
So many of my swift steeds;
You ignored my pleading words
And struck down, before my eyes,
My people as well.
You brazen bitch, you have chilled
The proud strength in my back.
Over narrow cliffs and rugged, arduous roads,
I have come to exact vengeance.
Bringing hardship, affliction, and strife,
Fighting tirelessly for six months,
You renowned woman, warrior maiden,
I have come to take revenge on you!
If you accept a fair settlement, bitch,
I have come to divide
The treasure of Kayypchal.
But if you bristle in fury,
I have come to fight day and night without fleeing,
Until one of us dies.
If you do not accept these words,
If you do not pay the blood-price,
I shall not let you sow your crops,
Break open the earth,
Or carry on your livelihood.
I bristle with fury;
You have sorely provoked my rage.
My very being thirsts for blood.
I shall die before suffering disgrace—
Mark well the words I speak,
And do not rouse my savage wrath;
Come against me, raging bitch!
Let it be said that mighty Kuyaly
Was taken by warrior Sarybay;
Let the dread banner of dominion be raised,
Let there be an uproar that rends the sky.
Let it win fame among every nation
And be a lesson to those who remain.
Red-robed maidens with moon-slender waists,
Let your beautiful leader of girls come forth;
Let your nimble young men come forth.
I shall take you all as plunder,
I shall slaughter every one of you!
My name is Sarybay,
And now my fierce rage is roused.
When wrath takes me, I stand unyielding;
I roar with menace,
And today I have summoned
The turmoil of the whole world.
My true fury has seized me;
If I do not utterly destroy your people,
If I do not make girls like you
My women upon the open steppe,
May I die unworthy of the name Sarybay,
May I sink into darkness as though never born!”
Thus Sarybay spoke,
And when he made that threat,
Her thoughts pierced and scattered,
A thousand grievous troubles
Pressed close upon her soul.
“I stand upright and free;
Driven by honor, wretched soul that I am,
I shall strike this wrathful infidel,
Who has inflicted such abundant sorrow;
I shall crush beneath my feet
Those other wretched wretches.
I shall utterly annihilate them
And slaughter their champions.
Sarybay is indeed an infidel;
I shall beat his far-famed fury from him.
After fighting fiercely for six months,
I shall find a way to settle his account.
I shall slaughter his renowned men;
And if my strength proves insufficient,
Let me die by this shameless dog!
Whatever venomous calamity and hardship
Descends upon my head, I shall face it.
If almighty Allah wills,
I shall submit to His command.
This precious, priceless golden life—
Sarybay is a tyrant,
So I shall surrender it to Sarybay.
At the funeral feast for my khan father,
Before the vast assembly,
I shall grapple and test myself
Against this savage enemy dog.
Dueling before the people,
I shall see how great his courage is.
How could I surrender my khan father’s treasure
And ever show my face again?
The sly boar seems to have gone mad;
I shall meet him squarely in battle
And now, once and for all,
Test myself against him!
Standing face-to-face,
Swinging axes and thrusting spears,
We shall clash and snarl in battle,
Making the whole world ring with our fame
And covering the earth in dust;
Thus shall I measure our strength.
The sly boar has gone mad;
Now, once and for all,
I shall test myself against him.
When he charged from that place,
He leaned back without losing strength
And came on in a frenzy.
If one falls into the infidel’s hands,
At the final end of time,
One’s mail will not remain whole,
Nor does he look inclined to spare a life.”
Thinking thus, she said:
“I shall press Zhelzhetpes with my thighs,
Take up my well-fashioned spear,
Turn my charger’s head,
And thrust my spear without delay.
The edge beside the lungs is the seam,
The place where throat, liver, and heart
Join together is the border.
That is the destined place;
The sovereign Allah is the one God,
And this is the moment
When the dreadful, monstrous foe must die.
If I strike downward by chance,
The Kalmyk saddle-bow is there;
If I thrust sideways by chance,
The head of the shoulder blade is there.”
Beneath her was the charger Zhelzhetpes;
Seizing the black-jawed whip
And wheeling it around,
She drew the woman-like swine
Off toward the flank,
Broke through the dead end, and opened a path.
Before one could say a word,
In the blink of an eye,
Before Sarybay, son of a monster,
Could turn his charger’s head,
She thundered out a battle cry;
The people fled before her menace.
If the great gate-like buckteeth bit down,
They would crush with a crack;
Unable to find their bearings,
The multitude fled in clamorous panic.
At the earth-bending boar
My impetuous fury flared;
I turned Zhelzhetpes’s head,
Caught him, and struck with my spear.
Before all the people, I charged
And speared the villain.
For seven days without rest
I battled the giant in fury.
Facing one another across the slope,
Exhausting ourselves with gunfire,
We fought in a bloody clash;
Every axe shattered with a crash,
And spears snapped with a shriek.
Hillocks and hollows were leveled,
And for mortal humankind
It became a deed never to be forgotten.
They grappled fiercely and hurled one another,
Beginning a grievous conflict;
Dust flew into the sky,
And the earth turned gray with haze.
The whole world was shaken;
Dust billowed over the hills,
And darkness filled the ravines.
The people surged in uproar,
And my ancient fury stirred.
The accursed world’s
Falseness was laid bare.
Before the frenzy of the infidel,
The monster’s son, no soul could stand;
The whole assembly despaired of life.
The furious conflict became a calamity,
And the multitude despaired of life.
The ravenous nature
Of the earth-crushing boar was revealed;
Blood gushed and was swallowed by the ground,
And the impenetrable mail
Was torn to shreds.
The towering black ribs
Were stripped apart layer by layer;
The monstrous nature
Of the swine, the monster’s son, was revealed.
Those with sense grieved,
While senseless men struck and stabbed blindly,
Crying, “None of us will survive now!”
And despairing of their precious lives.
Khans died in the collision,
And all who grappled died;
The place became one vast dug grave.
What an upright person witnessed
Was a seething mass of misery.
We clashed among the people,
Fighting beside the funeral feast;
I fought battle upon battle.
There among the multitude, the swine
Had sixty champions supporting him;
I slaughtered them where we fought.
We battled until our strength failed,
Struggling after the spears broke;
Without sleeping by day,
We fought for sixty days.
Innocent young men and khans died,
And blameless souls died.
People of many different nations died;
All who came to the feast died.
The war banner was raised,
And the sight became a grievous uproar.
I fought a fierce struggle
And began the slaughter in earnest.
This accursed but necessary life—
Though I was a maiden, for honor’s sake
I bound my precious, sugar-sweet soul
To a single hair and cast it aside.
I turned my heart toward death,
Girded my waist in the cause of honor,
And preserved my people.
My father was old, and I was a girl;
What other recourse was there against the swine?
Entangled with that monstrous brute,
At my khan father’s funeral feast,
Before the vast assembly,
He crushed the weak and forced a path,
Boasting himself a hero and a lion,
Claiming to be braver than every nation.
The rabid, fiery madman
Raged like a stallion
And lunged like a bull,
Taming a wild doe into a cow,
And displaying his bloodthirstiness.
Without cause or accusation,
He tormented the fly-like lives
Of the people who came to the feast,
Relentlessly heaping humiliation upon them.
When he began strife among the multitude
And reduced them to submission,
When he unleashed grievous conflict,
When the smiting God struck him,
I beat his age-old fury from him.
